summary: Separate the field itself from the numerical path traced through it, and keep the step size visible as a modelling choice.
objective: Build a vector field where I can drop a seed point, integrate its path with a chosen step size and compare the result against a refined reference.
intent_signals: Trace a particle path through a vector field and show how accurate it is.
Show how step size changes an integrated field line.
example_prompts: Build a 3D vector field with seed points, an integrated path and a step-size control.
Compare a coarse and a refined integration of the same field line.
negative_signals: Not a fluid solver: the field is prescribed, not computed from any physical equation.
Not a particle system with mass, drag or collisions.
not_for: Not a fluid solver: the field is prescribed, not computed from any physical equation.
Not a particle system with mass, drag or collisions.

entities.name: Field sampling
entities.guidance: Sample the field on a sparse lattice with arrows whose display scale is stated, since arrow length is a chosen gain and not a physical magnitude.

entities.name: Integrated path
entities.guidance: Draw the path as a polyline of actual integration steps with visible step markers, so the discretisation is inspectable rather than hidden by smoothing.

entities.name: Reference comparison
entities.guidance: Integrate the same seed with a much smaller step or a higher-order method and draw the divergence between the two paths.

state_contract.model: A prescribed analytic field, a seed position, a step size h, an integration method and a step count N with the horizon fixed as T = N h, so halving h doubles N and comparisons are made at matched times. The drawn path is the sequence of computed states; the reference path is a separately computed refinement, which is a numerical reference rather than truth.
state_contract.authority: The integrator output is authoritative for the path. Smoothing is display only and must never be used to hide step-to-step differences.
actions: Place or drag a seed point.
Change the step size and step count.
Switch integration method and compare against the reference.
Reset seeds, step size and camera.

invariants: For a smooth field already in the convergence regime, halving h while doubling N to hold T fixed reduces the error at matched times roughly in proportion to h for a first-order method. This is a conditional expectation, not a configuration test: a constant field is integrated exactly by Euler at every h, and pre-asymptotic or rounding-dominated regimes break the trend without any defect.
The path never leaves the domain where the field is defined without the scene reporting it.
At a point where the field vanishes the path stops advancing rather than drifting.
motion_guidance: Advance the integration in visible steps and allow stepping backwards through stored states rather than re-integrating with sign flipped.
Keep arrow scale fixed while the step size changes, so only the path changes.
known_limits: Illustrative error comparison only; no error bound, order verification or tolerance certification is claimed.
Streamlines of a time-dependent field are not particle trajectories, and this recipe uses a steady field to avoid that confusion.
Error behaviour is only expected in the asymptotic regime for a smooth field; step-size trends are illustrative and do not verify the order of a method.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Euler stepping approximates a scalar initial-value problem with x_n = x_(n-1) + h and y_n = y_(n-1) + h f(x_(n-1), y_(n-1)), evaluating the slope at the previous computed point.
claims.scope: Explicit Euler recurrence for a scalar initial-value problem as cited, applied componentwise to the prescribed 3D field. The claim does not guarantee monotonic error reduction under refinement; convergence-regime comparisons and reference accuracy are separately declared modelling conditions.

source_refs.locator: 4.2, Euler Method recurrence for x_n and y_n

claims.statement: A direction field represents solutions of a first-order differential equation graphically, and a solution curve is the graph of the solution to an initial-value problem.
claims.scope: Definition used here to distinguish the drawn field from the drawn path.

object_craft.structure: Cone-headed arrows of constant screen-relative width on a lattice whose spacing is a stated parameter.
object_craft.material: Neutral desaturated arrows so integrated paths keep the accent palette; magnitude is encoded by length and by a legend, not by hue alone.
object_craft.articulation: None. Arrows are rebuilt only when the field or lattice changes.

object_craft.structure: Tube along the polyline with spheres at each computed state, so the step count is countable at close range.
object_craft.material: One accent for the working path and a second, lower-value accent for the reference path.
object_craft.articulation: The path grows by appending states; scrubbing moves an index rather than re-integrating.

physical_contract.scope: Numerical integration of a prescribed field with an explicit step size; no masses, forces or contact.
driving: Field evaluation at the current state supplies the increment.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed step size chosen by the user; rendering interpolates only between stored states.
checks: Compare errors only at matched times with T fixed and a sufficiently accurate reference. Interpret first-order refinement trends only in the declared convergence regime before reference or rounding error dominates; lack of pairwise improvement alone is not failure. Report the constant-field case as exact in ideal arithmetic, subject to floating-point tolerance.
Reset clears stored states so no stale path remains.
